manifest.title: BBB gold-voter coverage and source-purity v4 audit
manifest.description: Technical audit of the BBB meaningful-CNS-access gold contract, apparent direct-record omissions, and the source-purity v4 correction.

blocks.body: # BBB gold-voter coverage and source-purity v4 audit

## Technical summary

**The L5 error is fixed without changing any gold label.** The reviewed external record is a comparative qualitative BBB statement, not an influx assay or a measured CNS-exposure experiment. Source-purity v4 moves it from L5 `influx_transport` to L2 `near-direct`. A full 581,708-row v3→v4 comparison found exactly one family change, zero moved gold voters, and zero family-safety violations. Preparation of all 398 conditioned validation rows found only Query 97 changed: the offending card is removed from L5, while the other 397 queries are evidence-equivalent.

**The impression that some direct records are missing is also valid.** The frozen gold contract is deliberately precision-oriented: among 304,845 frozen Starling rows, only 8,268 experimental records vote. In particular, 7,226 frozen-source rows passed the direct-outcome and experimental-basis gates but were rejected because they lacked an explicit binary permeability label. In the larger normalized retrieval universe, the analogous set contains 20,286 direct-scope rows. They are real measured or qualitative CNS outcomes, but the current gold builder refuses to invent a binary direction from heterogeneous measurements.

## One reviewed row moved from influx to near-direct

The affected source row is attached to the 4-amino analog and states that the query compound cannot penetrate the BBB while the analog crosses. It contains no influx assay, transporter-specific measurement, or primary CNS-exposure measurement. Therefore it is label-proximal evidence suitable for L2, but it is not eligible for experimental L1 or gold voting. The correction uses the stable canonical record ID, not a broad text keyword.

## A row must pass every gold gate before it can vote

A BBB source record votes only when it has a resolvable parent molecule; reports CNS access after systemic dosing with an intact or explicitly conditioned barrier; belongs to brain tissue, unbound brain, brain/systemic ratio, CSF, PET/autoradiography, or explicit in-vivo BBB outcome; has an explicit experimental basis; carries an explicit positive or negative `bbb_permeability_label`; and has no unresolved query/analyte, route, formulation, metabolite, or direction conflict. PAMPA, MDCK, predictions, mechanism-only transporter evidence, non-systemic delivery, and efficacy-only inference cannot vote. Parent labels then require at least 70% record agreement; exact ties and sub-70% conflicts are rejected.

## The main recall gap is explicit direction, not endpoint recognition

The 20,286 normalized-v7 rows below already pass the conditioned-compatible direct-outcome scope and experimental-basis checks. They remain outside L1 because the source supplies no explicit binary permeability label. Many contain useful measurements—brain concentration, Kp,uu, brain/plasma ratios, CSF ratios, or PET uptake—but their sign cannot be assigned using one universal threshold across dose, species, time point, formulation, and endpoint. This is a genuine high-precision versus recall trade-off rather than evidence that the endpoint parser failed to notice the measurements.

## Retrieval sees sources that frozen gold never considered

The frozen gold builder consumes only the pinned `starling-labs/BBB` source. The normalized retrieval library additionally contains passive-permeability, efflux, and influx acquisitions. Consequently, a retrieval card can be semantically close to the label yet have no possible gold-vote provenance. The corrected external record is one such row: it has `source_record_id=ext_1`, no frozen source index, and came from the influx acquisition.

## Method and robustness checks

The audit compared source-purity v3 and v4 row-for-row on `group_id`, rebuilt the physical-assay catalog and mechanism-tagged index from v4, and ran a prepare-only Query 97 smoke against the new index. The v4 index contains 22,958 physical assays, 37,411 molecules, and 172,518 assay×molecule rows. The corrected record is stored with `evidence_family=central_functional_access_proxy` and `evidence_family_level=2`; it is no longer available as a new L5 influx card. Gold artifacts were read only and their hashes were not modified.

## Limitations and uncertainty

The 7,226 frozen-source rejection count and 20,286 normalized-retrieval count are not row-for-row comparable: normalized-v7 includes cross-source acquisition, normalization, and duplicate representations. The 20,286-row census used conditioned-compatible scope, so some measurements require condition-specific rather than molecule-only labels. Finally, a direct measurement is not automatically an interpretable binary outcome; concentration and ratio thresholds depend on endpoint semantics and experimental context. No chart is used because the key evidence is an audit of distinct contracts and source universes, where an apparent funnel would be misleading.

## Recommended next step

Keep `experimental_meaningful_cns_access_v3` frozen for the current benchmark. Build a separate, lineage-pinned `experimental_metric_direction_review` over the 7,226 frozen-source rows rejected only for missing binary direction. Prioritize records with interpretable ratios or explicit restricted/adequate language, preserve condition and formulation context, and require endpoint-specific rules plus manual adjudication where a numeric threshold is not defensible. Only after parent-level revoting and split-impact auditing should any expanded gold lineage replace v3.

## Further questions

The remaining decision is whether the intended benchmark should optimize for a conservative, source-native binary label contract or for broader recovery of measured CNS exposure. The latter can increase coverage, but it creates a new labeling study rather than a retrieval-family bug fix.
